dedupe_keys.name: positionz continuously operating gnss reference stations toitu te whenua linz

description: PositioNZ is the network of Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand, with 37 continuously operating GNSS reference stations across New Zealand, including the Chatham Islands, and Antarctica, plus data from several other stations. It collects data from GPS, BeiDou, Galileo, GLONASS and QZSS. It is run with GNS Science through the GeoNet project, which monitors natural hazards, and its main purpose is to monitor the NZGD2000 geodetic datum and supply data for the national deformation model, keeping the datum aligned with the ITRF; six sites also feed the International GNSS Service. LINZ provides static RINEX data through the PositioNZ RINEX data archive, real-time RTCM streams through PositioNZ-RT, and a post-processing service, PositioNZ-PP, for positioning to a few centimetres. All data is free to reuse under the LINZ copyright licence terms. Caveats: the GNSS services are used through customer subscriptions, and the page itself gives the product links. Coverage is New Zealand and Antarctica. It supports positioning infrastructure studies, crustal deformation monitoring after earthquakes, and space weather effects on GNSS; related records are ReNEP of Portugal and ERGNSS of Spain.
